title: Signal Time
statement: A network has n relays, 0 to n − 1, and one-way links links[i] = [a, b, t]: a signal takes t milliseconds from a to b. A signal starts at relay 0. Return how long until every relay has received it, or −1 if some relay never does.

keyPoints: A min-heap of (time, relay), starting with (0, 0)
Pop the smallest time; skip relays already final
Answer: the largest final time, or −1 if a relay was never reached
edgeCases: Several links between the same relays
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Dijkstra with a linear scan for the minimum: O(V²)

hints: The links have different times, so the fewest links is not the fastest path. Which algorithm handles that?
Dijkstra: always finalize the relay with the smallest known time.
Use a min-heap; after it empties, the answer is the largest time, unless some relay is still unreached.
